label: REFINED-ADAPTATION / PROXY

reference_impl.alpha_definition: alpha = 1 + n/(sum(log(evals[i:])) - n*log(xmin)) for each candidate xmin=evals[i]; pick xmin minimizing KS distance D. Fit is on EIGENVALUES lambda=sigma^2.
reference_impl.blme_definition: alpha = 1 + k/sum(log(top_k/x_min)), k=round(0.2*len), x_min=top_k[-1].  Fit is on SINGULAR values sigma, fixed 20% tail (no KS xmin search).

check_a_known_exponent_recovery.generator: inverse-CDF power law p(sigma)~sigma^-a, xmin=1, N=5000
check_a_known_exponent_recovery.note: Hill alpha recovers the density exponent a within statistical error; tighter tail_fraction -> less bias, more variance.

check_c_blme_vs_ww_delta.interpretation: BLME alpha (on singular values, fixed 20% tail) is NOT equal to WW alpha (on eigenvalues, KS-optimal xmin).  The two differ by (i) the sigma-vs-lambda factor-2 scale [alpha_sigma ~ 2*alpha_lambda-1] and (ii) the fixed-tail-vs-KS-xmin choice.  The 'mapped' column removes (i); the residual is (ii).  Divergence is EXPECTED and documented; equality is NOT forced.
check_c_blme_vs_ww_delta.verdict: PROXY (kernel-exact vs independent Hill; NOT WW xmin-MLE alpha)

check_d_anchor_marchenko_pastur.band_derivation: HTSR eigenvalue band [2,6] mapped to sigma scale via alpha_sigma ~ 2*alpha_lambda - 1.
check_d_anchor_marchenko_pastur.note: Random (MP) layer -> LARGE alpha in both BLME and WW (no real heavy tail; sharp spectral edge). BLME(sigma)=7.865 and WW(lambda)=8.761 AGREE that this is a high-alpha random layer; BLME lands inside the sigma-scale [3,11] band.

verdict_detail: BLME's Hill kernel is EXACT vs an independent Hill transcription (<1e-9). It is NOT WeightWatcher's xmin-MLE alpha: WW scans all xmin candidates and picks the KS-optimal one on the eigenvalue ESD, whereas BLME uses a fixed 20% tail on singular values.  geometry_spectral is honestly a REFINED-ADAPTATION proxy of HTSR alpha; ranking-preserving but not value-comparable to published WW alpha.
